record.paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
record.original_question: In asymmetric Euclidean Ramsey notation, E^N ->_2 (X1, X2) means that every 2-coloring of E^N contains either a congruent copy of X1 in color 1 or a congruent copy of X2 in color 2. Let P2 be a two-point set whose points are distance 1 apart. The source records a set T8 of eight points in E^2 for which E^2 does not arrow (P2, T8). Is there a set T with fewer than eight points in E^2 such that E^2 has a 2-coloring with no color-1 copy of P2 and no color-2 copy of T?

evidence.quote: we denote this by E^N ->_2 (X1, X2)
There is a set T8 of 8 points in E^2
It is not known if there are sets with fewer than 8 points

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the Euclidean plane $E^2$. For finite point sets $X_1, X_2 \subset E^2$, write $E^2 \to_2 (X_1, X_2)$ to mean: for every 2-coloring $c : E^2 \to \{1,2\}$, either there exists a congruent copy of $X_1$ all of whose points receive color 1, or there exists a congruent copy of $X_2$ all of whose points receive color 2. Write $E^2 \not\to_2 (X_1, X_2)$ to denote the negation.

Let $P_2 \subset E^2$ denote any two-point set whose two points are at Euclidean distance $1$ apart. It is known that there exists a set $T_8 \subset E^2$ consisting of $8$ points such that $E^2 \not\to_2 (P_2, T_8)$.

Question: Does there exist a finite set $T \subset E^2$ with $|T| < 8$ such that $E^2 \not\to_2 (P_2, T)$? Equivalently, is there a 2-coloring of $E^2$ that contains no color-1 congruent copy of $P_2$ and no color-2 congruent copy of $T$, for some set $T$ of at most $7$ points?
artifact.status_search_result: The smallest known construction in the plane uses an 8-point set $T_8$ for which $E^2 \not\to_2 (P_2, T_8)$; related work (e.g., Arman–Tsaturian) addresses analogous configurations in higher-dimensional Euclidean spaces but does not establish a planar example with fewer than 8 points. No source found reports a planar construction with $|T|<8$, and the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A result in asymmetric Euclidean Ramsey theory
status_evidence.snippet: It is proved that if the points of the three-dimensional Euclidean space are coloured in red and blue, then there exist either two red points unit distance apart, or six collinear blue points with distance one between any two successive points.
status_evidence.claim: Recent asymmetric Euclidean Ramsey work treats higher-dimensional analogs but does not improve the planar bound below 8 points.

status_evidence.title: Euclidean Ramsey Theory (Handbook chapter 11)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Euclidean Ramsey theory including asymmetric arrow relations.
status_evidence.claim: Standard surveys record the 8-point construction without a smaller planar example.
